_comment: [OPUS-4.8] Competitor-comparison registry + dashboard seam (sq-t0c3). Authored by Opus 4.8
(Fable unavailable; flag for re-review when Fable returns).
TWO ROLES, one file:
1. REGISTRY (the `competitors` array): the versioned, pinned recipe for each external engine we
compare against — name, kind, pinned version, install/run recipe, which sparq suites it is
comparable on, and where its version+env metadata is recorded. This is the source-of-record
for `scripts/gather-competitors.sh` and for any human reproducing a comparison.
2. DASHBOARD SEAM (the top-level `engines` + `values` keys): the shape the perf dashboard
(bench/dashboard/dashboard.js, buildFeatured/competitorsFor/competitorEngines) reads to draw
competitor reference COLUMNS next to sparq in the featured-suites table. Shape (verified
against dashboard.js): { engines:[{id,label,version,env}], values:{ "<metric stem or name>":
{ "<engineId>": <number> } } }. The dashboard matches on the raw metric NAME first, then the
stem (name minus _us); a missing key renders as "—"/"n/a". We NEVER bake numbers in here by
hand — `values` ships EMPTY in git and is populated only by a real measured gather run (which
writes a sibling results file; see `results_layout`). Hard-coded perf numbers in a tracked
file are forbidden by AGENTS.md (No hard-coded performance numbers).
HONESTY NOTE (per parent sq-i0nm design C): competitor numbers gathered on a GitHub-hosted CI
runner are NOISY and not comparable to the pinned EC2/quiet-box reference band. Every gathered
datapoint records its `env` (host class, cpu, os, quiet_box flag) so the dashboard can label a
noisy gh-runner point distinctly from an EC2 reference line. See `bench/CATALOG.md` QUIET-BOX note.
Where gathered numbers + version/env metadata LAND. `scripts/gather-competitors.sh` writes a
results file (git-ignored, regenerable) per the conventions in bench/CATALOG.md — it does NOT
edit the `engines`/`values` below in git. A maintainer (or a scheduled job) reviews the results
file and, only if intended, commits a dashboard snapshot into `engines`/`values`.
results_layout.dashboard_snapshot: the top-level `engines` + `values` keys of THIS file (committed only deliberately, reviewed in-diff like bench/perf-baseline.json)

sparq_suite_catalog: bench/benchmarks.toml (machine-readable) + bench/CATALOG.md (human guide). Competitor `comparable_suites` below reference suite ids/dirs from that catalog.

competitors.name: Oxigraph
competitors.role: Differential-correctness oracle + mature-Rust-engine perf reference. Already a dev/bench dependency of this repo.
competitors.version_source: crates/sparq-bench/Cargo.toml (oxigraph = { version = "0.5", default-features = false, features = ["rdf-12"] }); resolved exact version pinned in Cargo.lock
competitors.install_recipe: none — built into the workspace via the `sparq-bench` crate; `cargo build -p sparq-bench --release`
competitors.run_recipe: cargo run -p sparq-bench --release -- --scale <entities> --iters <K>  (compare path: sparq vs Oxigraph on the in-process synthetic social graph, solution-count cross-check + per-query warm latency)

comparable_suites.note: head-to-head warm latency + solution-count agreement on the synthetic social graph
correctness only (no perf): differential fuzz vs Oxigraph
comparable in count mode on the SP2Bench corpus (load .nt into oxigraph::store::Store, run queries/)
comparable in count mode on the WatDiv SF=1 corpus
comparable on the BSBM Explore corpus (CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE forms compare produced-triple counts)
comparable on the DBPSB/FEASIBLE DBpedia cut
comparable on the LUBM extensional tier (Oxigraph has no OWL-RL reasoner — entailed tier is NOT comparable)

competitors.version_env_metadata: captured at gather time from Cargo.lock (exact resolved oxigraph version) + host env block; the sparq-bench compare path already prints both engines' load/query timings and peak RSS to stdout.

competitors.name: QLever
competitors.role: External on-disk engine reference (scales to billions; compressed on-disk index). Compared COLD, cache cleared each run; COUNT VALUES + result SIZES cross-checked, not just row==row.
competitors.version_source: bench/qlever-*/Qleverfile (IMAGE = docker.io/adfreiburg/qlever:latest). NOTE: `:latest` is NOT a pin — the gather script resolves and records the image DIGEST at run time (the digest IS the version identifier; compare.py reports no server build string); record that digest here when you fix a reference.
competitors.version_pin_followup: replace `:latest` with a sha256 digest pin in the Qleverfiles once a reference image is chosen — tracked as bead sq-l9yt.
competitors.install_recipe: docker pull docker.io/adfreiburg/qlever:latest  (or the qlever-control CLI: pipx install qlever; `qlever` reads a Qleverfile). Docker is NOT installed on the dev box — this competitor is gather-only on a box that has Docker.
competitors.run_recipe: in a bench/qlever-* dir: `qlever get-data && qlever index && qlever start`, then `python3 compare.py <iters> <endtoend|compute>` (drives sparq-cli AND the QLever HTTP endpoint; min-of-N cold).

comparable_suites.note: real skewed DBpedia/Wallscope olympics (~1.78M); compare.py compute|endtoend
WatDiv corpus via a Qleverfile (skewed-data tuning target — QLever's home turf)
BSBM Explore corpus via a Qleverfile
LUBM extensional tier (QLever does not materialize OWL-RL — entailed tier not comparable)

competitors.version_env_metadata: the gather script records (a) the resolved image DIGEST (`docker inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}'`) — this digest IS the recorded version identifier — and (b) the host env block. compare.py reports only timings + correctness, no server build string, so there is no separate 'server-reported version' to capture; `--run` refuses a live qlever gather when the digest cannot be resolved (no Docker / image not pulled) rather than writing an unversioned result. Stored QLever reference numbers + machine spec live in bench/qlever-baselines.md.
competitors.stored_baselines: bench/qlever-baselines.md (we do NOT re-run QLever every sparq iteration — re-measure only when its version or the dataset changes; record date + version there).

competitors.name: EYE (Euler Yet another proof Engine)
competitors.role: N3 reasoner reference: parse -> forward closure -> serialize. The sparq-reason inference suites are compared against EYE's closure (same pipeline).
competitors.version_source: bench/inference/eye-comparison.md (records the EYE version + SWI-Prolog version + install commit). `eye --version` at run time is the authoritative reported version.
competitors.install_recipe: no Homebrew formula; install from eyereasoner/eye install.sh at the pinned commit (saved-state .pvm via SWI-Prolog). EYE is NOT installed on the dev box — gather-only where `eye` is on PATH. Set EYE=/path/to/eye.
competitors.run_recipe: EYE=$HOME/.local/bin/eye SPARQ_CLI=target/release/sparq-cli bench/inference/eye-comparison.sh  (min-of-N wall seconds; emits the sparq-vs-EYE table). EYE on dt100k is ~hours — gated behind EYE_DT100K=1.

comparable_suites.note: socrates / DeepTaxonomy (dt1k,dt10k,dt100k) / anc500 / grid30 N3 closures
OWL-RL reasoning tier conceptually comparable, but EYE consumes N3 rules not OWL-RL builtins directly — not wired; tracked as bead sq-bzr7

competitors.version_env_metadata: gather records `eye --version`, the SWI-Prolog version, and the host env block; the cited third-party EYE measurements + machine spec live in bench/inference/eye-comparison.md.
